title: Frost
description: A model and execution-profile recommender: task analysis in, one deterministic Recommend policy, human or JSON out.
provenance: Authored on 2026-09-16 from the Go sources under cmd/ and internal/ after slice 1 was implemented, plus config/ examples and the README. Elements marked proposed come from docs/plans/active/model-router.md (slices 1a, 2, 3 and the later API/MCP note) and are not built; the router's Capacity placeholder and the examples/capacity jq converter exist but nothing in the executable consumes a snapshot yet. Evidence paths are pointers into this repository, not proof that a claim is still current.

boundaries.title: Deterministic core
boundaries.description: No environment, filesystem or network reads. Adapters produce the inputs and render the Decision.

boundaries.title: Public model evidence
boundaries.description: Neutral, source-attributed facts about models. Frost reads the file; a producer, not the router, knows the public sources.

boundaries.title: Operator-owned configuration
boundaries.description: What the operator can actually run and how to choose: profiles, labeled priors, latency classes, policy, pools, and the question set the analyzer is asked.

boundaries.title: Transient capacity (proposed)
boundaries.description: Ephemeral usage observations, produced outside Frost and read as a neutral snapshot. A snapshot cannot redefine profile-to-pool topology.

boundaries.title: The only network seam
boundaries.description: Task text leaves the machine here and nowhere else. The adapter owns transport, retries and validation.

boundaries.title: Explicit local records
boundaries.description: Recording is opt-in with --record because the record stores task text. Replay recomputes the policy from stored answers.

scenes.title: The big picture
scenes.description: One binary, one pure selection core, and the files and service around it.

scenes.title: One route, start to finish
scenes.description: A task enters through the CLI, is judged by the analyzer, decided by Recommend, and rendered; --record keeps the answers and --replay recomputes without the provider.

scenes.title: Inside Recommend
scenes.description: How a validated assessment becomes a Decision inside the pure core: read the distributions, apply hard constraints, decide adequacy from measurements or labeled priors, then order by the chosen objective and add alternatives. The CLI calls in and receives the Decision; config and catalog supply the contract types.

scenes.title: Who owns each input
scenes.description: Public model evidence, operator-owned configuration and the proposed transient capacity snapshot are separate inputs with separate owners; the router only sees their normalized types.

scenes.title: What the plan adds next
scenes.description: Planned, not built: a catalog producer (slice 1a), capacity-aware choice with an external CodexBar producer (slice 2), reproducible evaluation (slice 3), and later API and MCP adapters over the same Recommend boundary.
